interactions.label: A patient with heart failure reports waking up gasping for breath one to two hou

params.question: A patient with heart failure reports waking up gasping for breath one to two hours after falling asleep. This symptom is best explained by:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cerebral hypoperfusion causes confusion and dizziness (forward failure symptoms), not respiratory distress. Nocturnal gasping is a pulmonary symptom.

answers.text: Backward failure on the right side causing hepatic congestion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Right-sided backward failure causes hepatomegaly, ascites, and peripheral oedema — not pulmonary symptoms like nocturnal breathlessness.

answers.text: Backward failure on the left side causing fluid redistribution into the lungs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea occurs when lying flat redistributes fluid from the legs into the pulmonary circulation, raising capillary pressure and causing pulmonary congestion.

answers.text: Forward failure causing renal hypoperfusion and sodium retention

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Renal hypoperfusion contributes to chronic fluid retention, but the acute gasping on lying down is caused by pulmonary congestion from fluid redistribution — a left-sided backward failure mechanism.

overallFeedback.feedback: PND results from left-sided backward failure. When the patient lies flat, fluid redistributes from the legs into the pulmonary circulation, and the failing left ventricle cannot handle the increased return, causing pulmonary congestion and gasping.
Correct. PND is a hallmark of left-sided backward failure — fluid shifts from dependent areas into the lungs when the patient lies flat, overwhelming the compromised left ventricle.

interactions.label: What is the single most common cause of right heart failure in everyday clinical

params.question: What is the single most common cause of right heart failure in everyday clinical practice?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cor pulmonale is the most common cause of ISOLATED right heart failure, but in everyday practice, left heart failure causing secondary right ventricular overload is more common overall.
Pulmonary congestion from left heart failure raises pulmonary arterial pressure, progressively overloading the right ventricle. That is why biventricular failure is the pattern seen most often.
Primary pulmonary hypertension is an uncommon condition. Left heart failure is a far more prevalent cause of right heart failure in clinical practice.
Isolated tricuspid valve disease is relatively rare. Most tricuspid regurgitation is functional, occurring secondary to right ventricular dilatation from left heart failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: The narration emphasises that while cor pulmonale causes isolated right heart failure, left heart failure is the most common overall cause, because congestion on the left eventually overloads the right ventricle.

Correct. Left heart failure is the most common cause of right heart failure. Pulmonary congestion raises right ventricular afterload, leading to biventricular failure — the pattern you will encounter most frequently.

interactions.label: A patient with heart failure has an ECG showing an irregularly irregular rhythm

params.question: A patient with heart failure has an ECG showing an irregularly irregular rhythm with no identifiable P waves. Why is this arrhythmia particularly important in the context of heart failure?

answers.text: It always indicates an underlying ischaemic cause of heart failure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Atrial fibrillation can arise from many causes in heart failure, including valvular disease, hypertension, and cardiomyopathy — it does not specifically indicate ischaemia.

answers.text: It both causes and worsens heart failure, and requires stroke risk assessment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Atrial fibrillation has a bidirectional relationship with heart failure: it can cause HF and is worsened by it. Every patient with both conditions needs a CHA₂DS₂-VASc score to guide anticoagulation.

answers.text: It confirms that the patient has right heart failure rather than left

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: AF does not distinguish between left and right heart failure. It can occur in either type and reflects atrial remodelling from any cause of heart failure.

answers.text: It indicates that the patient's heart failure is in the early stages

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: AF is more common in established heart failure with significant atrial dilatation. Its presence suggests substantial cardiac remodelling, not early disease.

overallFeedback.feedback: Atrial fibrillation has a unique bidirectional relationship with heart failure — it both causes and worsens the condition. Every patient with both needs a CHA₂DS₂-VASc score to determine whether anticoagulation is indicated.
Correct. AF both causes and worsens heart failure, creating a vicious cycle. The combination of AF and HF raises stroke risk, making CHA₂DS₂-VASc scoring essential to guide anticoagulation decisions.

interactions.label: Diuretics are one of the four pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy in h

params.question: Diuretics are one of the four pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Diuretics are important for managing fluid overload symptoms, but they do NOT reduce mortality. The four pillars are RAAS blockers (ACEi/ARB/ARNI), evidence-based beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin). The narration notes that diuretics and digoxin 'don't extend survival the way these four pillars do.'
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Although diuretics are widely used for symptom relief in heart failure, they do not reduce mortality. The four mortality-reducing pillars are RAAS blockers (ACEi/ARB/ARNI), evidence-based beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and SGLT2 inhibitors.

interactions.label: An uncorrected atrial septal defect initially causes no cyanosis. What best expl

params.question: An uncorrected atrial septal defect initially causes no cyanosis. What best explains the absence of cyanosis?

answers.text: The defect is too small to allow significant blood flow

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Even large ASDs remain acyanotic initially. The absence of cyanosis depends on shunt direction, not defect size.

answers.text: Blood shunts from left to right, so only oxygenated blood recirculates

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Because left-sided pressures are normally higher, blood shunts left to right. Oxygenated blood recirculates through the lungs; no deoxygenated blood enters the systemic circulation, so there is no cyanosis.

answers.text: The right atrium prevents mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In ASD, blood freely crosses between the atria. The absence of cyanosis occurs because the shunt direction is left to right — oxygenated blood goes into the pulmonary circuit, not deoxygenated blood into the systemic circuit.

answers.text: Pulmonary blood flow is reduced, limiting oxygen desaturation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In acyanotic CHD with left-to-right shunts, pulmonary blood flow is actually INCREASED, not reduced. The extra volume overloads the lungs and right heart over time.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key determinant of cyanosis in congenital heart disease is shunt direction. In ASD, blood shunts left to right because left-sided pressures are higher. Only oxygenated blood recirculates — no deoxygenated blood reaches the systemic circulation, so there is no cyanosis.
Correct. In ASD, the left-to-right shunt means oxygenated blood recirculates through the pulmonary circuit. Since no deoxygenated blood escapes into the systemic circulation, there is no cyanosis.
